headline: High: Cursor can share local files and clipboard with Dify workflows, creating default-path prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads/writes workspace files and clipboard contents, and its shared state with other instances is via local filesystem. Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge base files and wire tools into agent/workflow flows. That creates a default path where attacker-controlled content from one side can be parsed as instructions by the other, with no provenance tracking shown.
conditions: IF Cursor writes untrusted content into a shared workspace file that Dify later ingests
IF Dify agent/workflow logic treats uploaded file text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace ingestion between the two systems
Require explicit human review before Dify consumes any Cursor-authored file
Use separate directories or volumes for each agent
Add provenance tags to all transferred files
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and broad network egress; Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs and can send data to model providers and user-defined tools. If the same sensitive file or clipboard content reaches both, either agent can forward it outside the local boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is opened in Cursor and uploaded to Dify
IF Dify is configured with external model providers or tools for that data
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared workspaces
Turn off clipboard-based transfer between agents
Restrict Dify to local/self-hosted providers for sensitive projects
Separate credentials and API keys per system
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on uploads and outbound tool calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem and execute_shell, and Cursor explicitly modifies git state while Dify can run server-side Python code and use tools. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes and git operations can race or overwrite each other, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Cursor auto-runs commands while Dify tools mutate the same files or git state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid git commits from both agents in the same branch
Use manual merge checkpoints
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code and modify files, while Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can act on tool outputs. If Dify consumes Cursor-produced text or code as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream actions or generated artifacts without a verification step shown in either profile.
conditions: IF Dify uses Cursor output as an input to an agent or workflow step
IF no explicit verification or test gate is inserted before Dify acts
mitigations: Insert a human approval step between agents
Require tests or linting before Dify consumes Cursor output
Limit Dify to read-only summarization of Cursor artifacts
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted until verified
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles clipboard contents and open files, while Dify stores conversation logs and knowledge base content. The profiles show different data classes and retention surfaces, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance risk is policy drift on the same sensitive data class rather than a proven regulatory breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from Cursor into Dify conversation logs or knowledge bases
IF the two systems have different retention or deletion policies for that data
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts
Set short retention on Dify logs
Use separate projects for regulated and non-regulated work
Review vendor data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems
